newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania to clamp down on tax evasion in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Albania to clamp down on tax evasion in 1997.

text.p: Albania's Prime Minister Aleksander Meksi said on Monday the government would try to increase revenues next year by launching a major drive against tax evasion, local news agency ATA reported.
Meksi said in an interview that tax evasion was the main source of the budget deficit.

"There is a deficit in the realisation of the revenues... (Taxes and revenues from customs) are the areas for which we are to work harder in the future," Meksi said, adding there would be no increase in taxes.
Albania's budget deficit in October was 10.0 percent of gross domestic product, according to latest figures from the the central Bank of Albania.
Meksi said Albania's economic growth had risen to 14 percent in 1996, compared with 13.4 percent a year ago, and described this as a major achievement of his government.
He said the government had passed a provisory three-month budget and would present the annual budget to parliament in January.

"Programmes of public investments have between two and three times higher funds from the World Bank, European Bank for Reconstruction and Development, European Investment Bank, Islamic Bank and other international institutions."
Meksi said the Albanian government was in the process of concluding an agreement with the International Monetary Fund and would strive for an association agreement with the European Union.

The prime minister said widespread get-rich-quick pyramid schemes had not affected inflation or the budget deficit but urged the people to deposit their money at banks, which he said were "more stable, successful and profitable for Albania".
